title: Spectre billiards ergodic
words: Billiards inside a spectre-shaped room with curved walls should be chaotic. Prove the billiard flow is ergodic.
math: Prove the billiard flow in the spectre (with its circular-arc edges) is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure.

title: Hats in a torus
words: Hats tile the plane only non-periodically, so they cannot tile a flat torus. Find the smallest uncovered fraction for packing hats on a flat torus of area A.
math: Let $g(A)$ be the least uncovered area over packings of congruent hats in flat tori of area $A$. Prove $g(A)\to\infty$ and determine its growth order in $A$.

title: Ramsey for square sums, three colours
words: Colour numbers with three colours; must some colour class contain two numbers summing to a square, three times over in a chain?
math: Prove every 3-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ has a monochromatic path of length 2 in $S_\infty$, i.e. $a,b,c$ of one colour with $a+b,\,b+c$ squares, $a<b<c$, and find the least $N$ forcing it in $[N]$.

title: Square-sum labelling of caterpillars
words: Label the vertices of a tree with 1 to n so that every edge sums to a perfect square. Show every caterpillar of maximum degree 3 can be done, once it is large.
math: Prove every caterpillar with $n\ge n_0$ vertices and maximum degree $\le3$ admits a bijection $V\to[n]$ with $\ell(u)+\ell(v)$ a square for every edge $uv$.

title: Hat tilings avoid squares
words: Show that in any hat tiling, the centres of four tiles never form a perfect square, or find the smallest one.
math: Decide whether four tile centres in some hat tiling form the vertices of a square; if so, determine the minimal side length over all hat tilings.

title: Many loops for affine prime maps
words: Show the number of separate loops of p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + 1 grows without bound as a grows.
math: Let $N(a)$ be the number of periodic orbits of $p\mapsto P(ap+1)$ on primes. Prove $\limsup_{a\to\infty}N(a)=\infty$.

title: Hat-tiling site percolation is irrational
words: The critical probability for percolation on the hat tiling is about 0.5442. Prove it is irrational.
math: Prove $p_c^{\mathrm{site}}$ of the hat-tiling dual graph is irrational.

title: Hot spots on the hat
words: Heat a hat-shaped insulated plate. Decide whether the hottest point eventually sits on the boundary.
math: Decide whether a second Neumann eigenfunction of the hat polygon attains its maximum only on $\partial\Omega$.

title: Thue–Morse meets Rudin–Shapiro on primes
words: Two classic ±1 patterns, Thue–Morse and Rudin–Shapiro, should be independent along the primes. Prove it.
math: Prove $\sum_{p\le x} t(p)\,r(p)=o(\pi(x))$, where $t$ is the Thue–Morse and $r$ the Rudin–Shapiro sequence.

title: Undecidable prime-factor maps
words: Show no algorithm can decide, given a and b, whether every orbit of n ↦ n/2 (even) or the largest prime factor of an + b (odd) eventually loops.
math: Prove $\{(a,b)\in\mathbb{N}^2:$ every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ ($n$ even), $P(an+b)$ ($n$ odd) is eventually periodic$\}$ is not recursive, or prove it is.

title: Hamiltonian cycles in hat patches
words: Count closed tours visiting every tile of a large hat-tiled region once. Find the exponential growth rate per tile.
math: For hat-tiled $L$-balls with $n$ tiles, prove $(\#\text{Hamiltonian cycles})^{1/n}\to\beta$ and determine $\beta$ to 3 digits rigorously.

title: Square-sum cover time
words: A random walker on the square-sum graph visits every number up to N. How long does it take?
math: For simple random walk on the giant component of $S_N$, prove the cover time is $(c+o(1))N^{3/2}\log N$ in expectation and find $c$.

title: Spectre chromatic number of distances
words: Colour points of the plane so no two points at a distance equal to a spectre edge length or diagonal share a colour. Find the colours needed.
math: Let $D$ be the set of distances between vertices of the spectre polygon. Determine $\chi(\mathbb{R}^2;D)$.

title: Pólya's conjecture for the hat
words: Pólya proved his eigenvalue lower bound for shapes that tile by translations. The hat tiles only with rotations and reflections, and only aperiodically. Prove the bound for the hat anyway.
math: Prove $\lambda_k(\Omega)\ge \frac{4\pi k}{|\Omega|}$ for all Dirichlet eigenvalues of the hat polygon $\Omega$.

title: Four-term square-sum chains in primes
words: Find infinitely many chains of four primes where each neighbouring pair sums to a square.
math: Prove infinitely many 4-tuples of primes $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ with $p_i+p_{i+1}$ a square for $i=1,2,3$.

title: Hearing the hat
words: Show no other polygon has exactly the same vibration frequencies as the hat.
math: Prove the hat polygon is Dirichlet-spectrally determined among all simply connected polygons.

title: Few loops for square-plus-one
words: The square-plus-one map has a loop: 89 goes to 233 and back. Show there are only finitely many loops.
math: Prove $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$ has finitely many periodic orbits (one is $89\leftrightarrow233$).

title: The spectre is not spectral
words: Show the spectre, a curved tile that cannot tile by translations, has no orthogonal basis of exponentials, as Fuglede's conjecture predicts.
math: Prove there is no $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $\{e^{2\pi i\lambda\cdot x}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is an orthogonal basis of $L^2$ of the spectre domain.

title: Square-sum clique minors
words: Find the largest complete graph that can be formed by contracting parts of the square-sum graph.
math: Determine the order of growth of the Hadwiger number $h(S_N)$.

title: Injective but not surjective, real
words: Find a polynomial map of 3D real space with determinant 1 everywhere that is one-to-one but misses some points.
math: Find $F\in\mathbb{R}[x,y,z]^3$ with $\det DF\equiv1$, $F$ injective on $\mathbb{R}^3$ but not surjective, or prove none exists.

title: Keller maps over the reals, surjectivity
words: Show some real 3D Keller counterexample is surjective as a map of real space.
math: Find a polynomial map $F:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$ with $\det DF\equiv1$ that is surjective but not injective, or prove none exists.

title: Turán density of the triangle-of-triangles
words: Find how many triples a 3-uniform hypergraph can have without containing a specific six-vertex configuration.
math: Determine $\pi(F)$ for the 3-graph $F$ on $[6]$ with edges $\{123,345,561,246\}$.

title: Square-sum Ramsey of paths
words: Two-colour the numbers 1 to N. Show some colour contains a chain of length L where neighbours sum to squares, with L growing like a power of N.
math: Prove every 2-colouring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic path in $S_N$ of length $\ge N^{c}$ for some $c>0$, and find the optimal $c$.

title: Linnik for seven-free primes
words: Show the smallest seven-free prime in an arithmetic progression is at most a fixed power of the modulus.
math: Prove there is $C$ such that for every $q$ and $(a,q)=1$ (with $10\nmid q$-compatibility conditions) there is a 7-free prime $p\equiv a\ (q)$, $p\le q^C$.

title: Gerver's constant is not a period
words: Show the area of Gerver's sofa cannot be written as an integral of an algebraic function over an algebraic region.
math: Prove $\mu_G\approx2.2195$ is not a Kontsevich–Zagier period.

title: Max-cut of the square-sum graph
words: Split the numbers up to N into two groups to cut as many square-sum pairs as possible. Find how far above one half you can get.
math: Prove $\mathrm{MaxCut}(S_N)=\big(\tfrac12+(c+o(1))N^{-1/4}\big)e(S_N)$ and determine $c$.

title: Tangent-sweep universality
words: Every known Jacobian-conjecture counterexample in 3D comes from sweeping tangent lines of a curve. Prove all of them do, up to coordinate changes.
math: Prove every non-invertible Keller map $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ is, up to composition with polynomial automorphisms on both sides, of tangent-sweep type.

title: Discrete sofa
words: Slide and rotate a polyomino by unit steps and quarter turns around the corner of a corridor k cells wide. Find the largest area possible, asymptotically.
math: Let $D(k)$ be the maximal number of cells of a polyomino that can pass the width-$k$ L-shaped corridor of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ by unit translations and $90^\circ$ rotations about lattice points (staying inside at all times). Prove $D(k)\sim ck^2$ and find $c$.

title: Greedy independent sets in square sums
words: Pick random numbers up to N one by one, skipping any that sum to a square with something already picked. How many do you end with?
math: Determine the asymptotic size of the random greedy independent set in $S_N$, in probability.

title: Prime-power Collatz
words: Halve even numbers; for odd n, divide 3n + 1 by its largest prime-power factor. Show every orbit reaches 1.
math: Let $c(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even), $c(n)=(3n+1)/q(n)$ ($n$ odd), $q(m)$ the largest prime power dividing $m$. Prove every orbit reaches $1$.

title: Lean proof of RH, halved
words: The 2026 Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis is 17 million lines. Produce one under 8 million lines on top of the same Mathlib.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` using at most $8\times10^6$ lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Prime Nim values stay small
words: Prime Nim's Grundy values grow incredibly slowly. Show they are at most a constant times log n.
math: For the subtraction game with prime moves, prove $G(n)=O(\log n)$.

title: Prime points on a quartic threefold
words: Count prime solutions of x⁴ + y⁴ + z⁴ = w⁴ + 2 up to size X, and find the asymptotic.
math: Find the asymptotic number of prime 4-tuples $\le X$ with $x^4+y^4+z^4=w^4+2$, or prove there are finitely many.

title: Hat dominoes freeze
words: Random domino-style pairings of hat tiles inside a large region with a fixed boundary develop a frozen outer zone. Find the shape of the boundary between frozen and random regions.
math: For uniform perfect matchings of the hat graph on regions $L\cdot\Omega$, prove an arctic curve exists and identify it for $\Omega$ a regular hexagon.

title: Seven-free primes as an additive basis
words: Show every large number is a sum of a bounded number of seven-free primes.
math: Prove there is $k$ such that every sufficiently large integer of suitable parity is a sum of at most $k$ primes with no decimal digit 7, and give an explicit $k$.

title: Spectre self-avoiding walks
words: Find the exponential growth rate of non-self-intersecting walks on the spectre tiling, and show it is the same for every spectre tiling.
math: Prove the connective constant $\mu$ of the spectre adjacency graph exists, is the same for all spectre tilings, and is not algebraic of degree $\le2$.

title: Keller maps with bounded fibres
words: Find the smallest possible maximum fibre size for a 3D Keller counterexample over the complex numbers.
math: Determine $\min\{\max_{y}|F^{-1}(y)|: F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3\text{ non-invertible Keller}\}$.

title: Affine prime maps, quantitative
words: Show that for the map p ↦ largest prime factor of 3p + 4, almost every prime reaches its loop within about log log p steps.
math: For $p\mapsto P(3p+4)$, prove that for all but $o(\pi(x))$ primes $p\le x$ the orbit of $p$ enters its (unique observed) 7-cycle within $C\log\log p$ steps.

title: Lonely runner gap for the first n primes
words: For the first n primes as speeds, find the actual loneliness gap asymptotically.
math: Determine the asymptotics of $\delta_n=\sup_t\min_{i\le n}\|tp_i\|$ as $n\to\infty$.

title: Long progressions of seven-free primes
words: Show the seven-free primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
math: Prove for every $k$ there are $k$-term arithmetic progressions consisting of primes with no decimal digit 7.

title: Primitive seven-free sets
words: Among sets of seven-free numbers in which no member divides another, show the seven-free primes maximise the sum of 1/(n log n).
math: Prove $\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{a\log a}\le\sum_{p\ \text{7-free prime}}\frac1{p\log p}$ for every primitive set $A$ of 7-free integers $>1$.

title: Maker–Breaker square-sum triangles
words: Maker and Breaker alternately claim numbers. Maker wins by owning three numbers whose pairwise sums are all squares. Decide who wins on 1 to N for large N.
math: Determine the winner of the Maker–Breaker game on $[N]$ whose winning sets are the triangles of $S_N$, for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Keller monodromy is everything
words: Show every symmetric group appears as the hidden symmetry group of the fibres of some 3D Jacobian-conjecture counterexample.
math: Prove that for each $n\ge3$ there is a non-invertible Keller map $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ of geometric degree $n$ whose generic monodromy group is $S_n$.

title: Hat tiling heat kernel constant
words: For a random walk on a hat tiling, find the exact constant in the return probability.
math: Prove $p_{2n}(o,o)\sim\frac{c(o)}{n}$ on the hat graph and show $\frac1{|B_R|}\sum_{o\in B_R}c(o)\to c$ with $c=\frac{\bar d}{2\pi\sqrt{\det\Sigma}}$, computing $\Sigma$ in closed form.

title: Cube-sum giant component
words: Join numbers summing to a cube. Show one piece eventually contains almost everything.
math: Prove the largest connected component of $C_N$ has $N-o(N)$ vertices.

title: Kissing numbers of polykite families
words: Show the hat's family of shapes has a kissing number that jumps at exactly one parameter value.
math: For Tile$(a,b)$, $a,b>0$, let $k(a,b)$ be the kissing number (congruent copies, reflections allowed). Prove $k$ is piecewise constant with finitely many jumps and find them.

title: Square-sum connectivity
words: Show the square-sum graph cannot be split by removing fewer vertices than its smallest degree.
math: Prove $\kappa(S_N)=\delta(S_N)$ for all large $N$.

title: Seven-free Chen primes in progressions
words: Show infinitely many seven-free primes p in every allowable residue class have p + 2 with at most three prime factors.
math: For each $q$ and admissible $a$, prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p\equiv a\ (q)$ with $\Omega(p+2)\le3$.

title: Arithmetic progressions in hat centres
words: Show any positive fraction of hat tiles contains three tiles whose centres are equally spaced on a line.
math: Prove every $A\subseteq$ (hat tile centres) of positive upper density contains $a,a+d,a+2d$, $d\ne0$.

title: Monochromatic square-sum triangles, many colours
words: Colour the positive integers with any finite number of colours. Show there are always three numbers of one colour whose pairwise sums are all squares.
math: Prove that for every $r$ and every $r$-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there are distinct $a,b,c$ of one colour with $a+b,a+c,b+c$ all perfect squares.

title: Seven-free squares
words: Count the numbers up to x whose square has no digit 7. Show the count matches the random-digit prediction.

title: Strict convexity of hat first-passage
words: Give each hat-tile edge an independent random length. Prove the limiting ball of first-passage distances is strictly convex.
math: For i.i.d. continuous edge weights with finite exponential moment on the hat adjacency graph, prove the first-passage limit shape exists and is strictly convex.

title: Prime-indexed seven-free primes
words: List the primes in order. Show infinitely many seven-free primes sit at a prime position in that list.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p_q$ with $q$ prime and $p_q$ free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Turán density with a twist
words: Same question for a seven-vertex configuration of five triples arranged around a central triple.

title: Partition numbers contain a 7
words: Show that from some point on, every partition number has a 7 among its digits.
math: Prove there is $N$ such that the decimal expansion of $p(n)$ contains the digit 7 for all $n\ge N$.

title: Prime Nim game graph
words: Prime Nim has losing positions with a hidden mod-structure. Show the losing positions are equidistributed in residue classes mod 3.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0,\ n\equiv a\ (3)\}\sim\frac13\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0\}$ for each $a$.

title: Seven-free Beatty primes
words: Show infinitely many primes of the form ⌊n√2⌋ contain no digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p=\lfloor n\sqrt2\rfloor$ with no decimal digit 7.

title: Square-plus-one orbits rarely loop
words: Show almost every starting number's square-plus-one sequence never repeats.
math: Prove the set of $n$ whose orbit under $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$ is eventually periodic has natural density 0.

title: Midpoint-prime Collatz
words: Halve even numbers; replace an odd number by the average of itself and the next prime. Prove every start reaches 1.
math: Let $m(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $m(n)=\tfrac12(n+p^+(n))$ for odd $n$, with $p^+(n)$ the least prime $>n$. Prove every orbit reaches $1$.

title: The 4p+1 funnel, almost always
words: Show almost every prime falls into the eight-prime loop of the 4p + 1 map.
math: Prove the set of primes whose $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$ orbit enters the 8-cycle has relative density 1 among primes.

title: Square-plus-one ladder
words: Start at 2. Repeatedly square, add one, and keep only the largest prime factor: 2, 5, 13, 17, 29, 421, … Show this sequence never settles down.
math: Let $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$, $P$ = largest prime factor. Prove the orbit $(Q^k(2))_{k\ge0}$ is unbounded.

title: Prime-sum Latin rectangle
words: Build a k × N table using each number 1 to N once per row, so adjacent entries in a row and in a column always sum to primes. Find the largest k possible for large N.
math: Determine $\limsup_{N}k(N)$ where $k(N)$ is the largest $k$ admitting a $k\times N$ array whose rows are permutations of $[N]$ with all horizontally and vertically adjacent sums prime.

title: Seven-free values of n²+1
words: Show infinitely many n make n² + 1 a prime with no digit 7, or at least a product of two such primes.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $n^2+1=q_1q_2$, $q_i$ primes free of the digit 7.

title: Seven-free Carmichael quotients
words: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers n have n − 1 seven-free.
math: Prove infinitely many Carmichael numbers $n$ such that $n-1$ has no decimal digit 7.

title: Waring with seven-free cubes
words: Find the fewest cubes of seven-free numbers needed to write every large number, and prove it.
math: Determine the least $s$ such that every sufficiently large integer is a sum of $s$ cubes of positive 7-free integers.

title: Square Nim from both ends
words: Two piles; a move removes a square from one pile or the same square from both. Find the losing positions' asymptotic density.
math: For moves $(a,b)\to(a-k^2,b),(a,b-k^2),(a-k^2,b-k^2)$, prove $\#\{(a,b)\in[N]^2:\mathcal P\}=N^{1+\theta+o(1)}$ and find $\theta$.

title: Antiferromagnetic hats
words: Colour hat tiles up or down to minimise same-colour neighbours. The hat graph has odd cycles, so some frustration is unavoidable. Compute the ground-state entropy exactly.
math: For the antiferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph, prove the zero-temperature entropy per tile exists, is positive, and compute it in closed form.

title: Prime-sum labelling of balanced trees
words: Label a tree with 1 to n so every edge sums to a prime. Parity forces the two sides of the tree to be balanced. Show balance is enough, for large n.
math: Prove every tree on $n\ge n_0$ vertices whose bipartition classes have sizes $\lceil n/2\rceil,\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ admits a bijection $V\to[n]$ with all edge sums prime.

title: Unit distances in three dimensions after 2026
words: The 2026 number-field idea beat Erdős in the plane. Adapt it to unit distances among points on a sphere in 3D.
math: Prove there are $n$-point sets on the unit sphere $S^2$ with $\ge n^{1+c}$ pairs at distance $1$, for some $c>0$ and infinitely many $n$.

title: Three loops for 2p+3
words: Under p ↦ largest prime factor of 2p + 3, every tested prime ends in one of three loops. Prove there are no others.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(2p+3)$ on primes enters one of the cycles $\{3\}$, $\{5,13,29,61\}$, $\{43,89,181,73,149\}$.

title: Irrationality of the hat percolation threshold, bond
words: The bond-percolation threshold on the hat tiling's edges is about 0.7982. Prove it is irrational.
math: Prove $p_c^{\mathrm{bond}}$ for the hat tiling's edge graph is irrational.

title: Increasing largest prime factors
words: Among P(1), …, P(N), the largest prime factors of 1 to N, find the longest strictly increasing subsequence. Show it grows like a power of N.
math: Let $L(N)$ be the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $(P(n))_{n\le N}$. Prove $L(N)=N^{\theta+o(1)}$ and find $\theta$.

title: Forced MHD blow-up with no field
words: Show viscous, resistive magnetic fluid can blow up from rest, with no magnetic field at the start, under a smooth push on the velocity alone.
math: For 3D incompressible viscous resistive MHD with $u_0=0$, $b_0=0$ and smooth compactly supported forcing in the momentum equation only, construct finite-time blow-up of $\|b\|_{L^\infty}$.

title: Bootstrap percolation on hats
words: Infect each hat tile at random with small probability p; a tile catches the infection once two neighbours have it. Find the exact scale at which a large region gets fully infected.
math: For 2-neighbour bootstrap percolation on hat-tiled $L$-balls, prove $p_c(L)\sim \lambda_{\mathrm{hat}}/\log L$ and determine $\lambda_{\mathrm{hat}}$.

title: Square-plus-one merging
words: Many square-plus-one sequences run into the one starting at 2. Decide whether every sequence eventually does, apart from those caught in loops.
math: Decide whether every $n\ge2$ whose $Q$-orbit is not eventually periodic satisfies $Q^a(n)=Q^b(2)$ for some $a,b$.

title: Shuffle orders hit every residue
words: The order of the three-pile shuffle on 3n cards takes every value modulo 4 infinitely often. Prove it.
math: With $\sigma_n$ the 3-pile out-shuffle, $\operatorname{ord}(\sigma_n)=\operatorname{ord}_{3n-1}(3)$; prove each residue class mod 4 is hit for infinitely many $n$.

title: Hat-tiling Sudoku impossibility
words: Try to label every hat tile with one of seven symbols so that each tile and its neighbours never repeat a symbol. Decide whether some hat tiling allows it.
math: Decide whether some hat tiling's adjacency graph admits a 7-colouring in which every closed neighbourhood is rainbow (a perfect $L(1,1)$-type colouring).

title: Spectre quantum walk spreading
words: A quantum particle hopping on the spectre tiling should spread at a rate strictly between localization and free motion. Compute the exponent.
math: For $H$ the adjacency operator of a spectre tiling and $\psi_0=\delta_o$, prove $\langle|X|^2\rangle_T\asymp T^{2\beta}$ and determine $\beta$.

title: Pólya's conjecture for the spectre
words: Prove Pólya's Neumann eigenvalue upper bound for the spectre, a curved shape that tiles only aperiodically.
math: Prove $\mu_{k+1}(\Omega)\le\frac{4\pi k}{|\Omega|}$ for all Neumann eigenvalues of the spectre domain $\Omega$.

title: Squares of seven-free primes
words: Show infinitely many primes have no digit 7 in themselves or in their squares.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with neither $p$ nor $p^2$ containing the decimal digit 7.

title: Gerver sofa contact points
words: Prove Gerver's sofa touches the corridor walls in exactly the pattern Gerver described at every moment of its optimal motion, and that the motion is unique.
math: Prove the optimal motion of Gerver's sofa through the unit corridor is unique up to time reparametrization.

title: Digit-restricted Chowla
words: Show μ(n)μ(n+1) has no bias on numbers n where neither n nor n+1 contains the digit 7.
math: Prove $\sum_{n\le x,\ 7\notin n,\ 7\notin n+1}\mu(n)\mu(n+1)=o(x^{\log9/\log10})$.

title: Tile(1,1) frieze
words: Decide whether Tile(1,1) can tile an infinite strip.
math: Decide whether Tile(1,1) tiles some strip $\mathbb{R}\times[0,w]$ using orientation-preserving isometries.

title: Odd runs of the midpoint map
words: How long can the midpoint-prime map stay on odd numbers? Show the runs can be arbitrarily long.
math: Prove that for every $L$ there is an odd $n$ with $m^j(n)$ odd for $0\le j\le L$.

title: Primes with balanced binary digits
words: Show infinitely many primes have exactly as many 1s as 0s in binary.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ whose binary expansion (of even length) has equally many 0s and 1s.
